source.source_manifest_algorithm: bootstrap-companions.py manifest schema_version=1; compact sorted-key SHA-256 of path, file SHA-256, byte size and executable-bit records; source exclusions follow the Hub companion manifest rules

frozen_snapshot.verified_independently: Two source_manifest_for content rechecks matched the ordered 254-file record and source SHA-256 after rebinding only the manifest path to the frozen snapshot.

runtime_floor.browser_consumers: caller-owned browser with normal Fetch, CORS and TLS validation

payload.artifact_verification: The retained local npm archive reproduced the recorded 81-member package SHA-256 and entry hashes. This handoff did not rebuild the SDK, start a consumer, or rerun the full package suite.

selectors.service_ownership: The SDK is imported by a caller-owned Node process; it owns no service, listener, data directory or service-manager registration.
selectors.target: A fresh caller-owned consumer root; do not install the SDK as Hub, Viewer, Home Assistant or Edge service.
selectors.evidence: Primary packed Debian ARM64 Node consumer and exact package identity are recorded in the SDK STATUS; this selector is not installed-service acceptance.
selectors.acceptance_receipt: Verify archive/member/entry identity, install into an isolated consumer root, import the public Node entry, record caller process ownership and remove only that consumer root.

selectors.service_ownership: The SDK supplies browser modules only; the browser, origin, TLS trust, CORS policy and hosting process remain caller-owned.
selectors.target: A fresh caller-owned browser consumer; no SDK listener or browser profile is retained by the aggregate component.
selectors.evidence: Primary Viewer/browser and installed Viewer data-state receipts bind the package identity, but do not promote this selector to a complete installed matrix cell.
selectors.acceptance_receipt: Verify archive/member/entry identity, load the browser entry from an isolated consumer, record normal TLS/CORS and caller process ownership, then remove only the consumer artifacts.

selectors.service_ownership: Developer-resource use only; no LaunchAgent, daemon, listener, pairing store or Hub administration service is supplied.
selectors.target: Fresh caller-owned Node/browser consumer root after the selected host supplies the pinned runtime.
selectors.acceptance_receipt: Source/package identity, public imports, caller-owned process lifecycle and cleanup; any later installed matrix proof is separately runner-owned.

selectors.service_ownership: Developer-resource use only; no systemd unit, daemon, listener, pairing store or Hub administration service is supplied.
selectors.target: Fresh authorized consumer host required; no retained or quarantined guest is substituted.
selectors.acceptance_receipt: Source/package identity, public imports, caller-owned process lifecycle and cleanup; installed Node/browser matrix evidence remains pending.

selectors.service_ownership: Blocked: the TypeScript SDK is a library/developer resource and does not own a service payload, service manager registration, listener, Hub storage, collector, pairing administration or aggregate activation.
selectors.blocked_reason: Do not select the SDK as a Hub/Viewer/Home Assistant/Edge service or infer installed acceptance from the package archive.
selectors.acceptance_receipt: Not applicable; service acceptance belongs to the owning product and the Hub aggregate runner.

ownership.code: The SDK owns its public client, generated types, validators, package metadata, examples, tests and developer documentation.
ownership.credentials: Credentials, invitations, bearer tokens, trust material and browser session state remain caller-owned and are never persisted by the SDK package.
ownership.data: The SDK owns no Hub database, TeslaMate source, vehicle data store, collector spool, pairing registry or durable telemetry state.
ownership.service: The SDK owns no daemon, LaunchAgent, systemd unit, Docker service, listener or service-manager registration. Hub owns aggregate selection and activation.
ownership.process: The importing Node process, browser page, origin and any test server are caller-owned; SDK process exit is not a service lifecycle receipt.
ownership.removal: Remove only the SDK archive/package from the selected consumer root; preserve Hub, Viewer, Home Assistant, Edge, credentials, databases and unrelated listeners.

lifecycle.select: Bind the developer-resource selector to the exact source manifest, profile identity, package SHA-256, member count and entry hashes before staging.
lifecycle.install: Copy the retained archive into a fresh caller-owned consumer root, verify its digest and package surface, and install without changing a service or sibling component.
lifecycle.start: There is no SDK start action: the caller imports the root, Node or browser entry and owns the process or page.
lifecycle.restart: Restart only the caller-owned consumer process or page; no SDK supervisor, listener or service state exists to restart.
lifecycle.upgrade: Retain the prior consumer package until the new archive and public imports are verified; rollback changes only the caller-owned consumer root.
lifecycle.uninstall: Remove only the SDK package and consumer-owned generated output; do not purge service data, credentials, Hub state or browser profiles.
lifecycle.runtime: Hub endpoint, TLS/CORS, browser hosting, credential lifecycle and any live-read receipt are external caller/Hub responsibilities.

receipt_schema.secret_policy: Never record invitation URIs, bearer/access tokens, device identifiers, private keys, certificate or CA bytes, browser profile databases, raw Hub response bodies, opaque cursors, or credential-bearing headers. Record only redacted statuses, digests, bounded counts, process results and listener ownership facts.
receipt_schema.acceptance_rule: This source handoff, frozen snapshot and archive check establish only a selectable developer resource. They do not promote any selector to installed service, live Hub, browser, Docker, passive-parity or cross-platform acceptance.

redaction_limits: The external manifest, frozen snapshot and package archive are owner-only local artifacts and are not repository publication artifacts.
The handoff records public artifact identities and ownership boundaries only; it contains no credential, invitation, trust secret, browser state, vehicle identity or raw response data.
No Hub, Viewer, Home Assistant or Edge service was edited, started, restarted, stopped or inspected as part of this handoff.
No Docker image, native package, service registration, installed target or live runtime receipt is claimed.
hub_action_requested: Verify the external owner-only SDK manifest and frozen snapshot twice, verify the retained 81-member package archive and exact profile/package identities, then bind the SDK only as an optional developer resource in the aggregate D1 manifest. Keep service selectors blocked and do not mutate a host, service, credential store or sibling component from this handoff.
